sources.title: Common juniper: selected multistemmed habit
sources.scope: Selected actual university species diagnosis through search retrieval: variable shrubby/tree habit, awl leaves in whorls of three with one broad pale upper band, globose wax-bloomed blue/black fleshy seed cones. No ordinary flower/fruit interpretation.

retrieval.accessMethod: Selected institutional botanical description through web retrieval; local HTML cached

findings.shape: A selected multistemmed juniper has irregular strip-bark stems, stiff spreading awl leaves in alternating whorls of three with one pale upper-band cue, and small fused fleshy blue-grey seed cones with a muted wax-bloom appearance.
findings.surface: Original numerical connected woody/green axes, individual curved leaf surfaces, subdued pigment variation and selected reproductive surfaces. No source photograph pixels or measured tissue optical parameters.
findings.movement: Same retained woody axes, rachises, leaves and reproductive surfaces during small authored external deflection. Root/support position and scale remain anchored. Timing and angles are qualitative; there is no wind/elasticity solver, physiological simulation or measured biomechanics. Complete germination, organ emergence and seed-to-adult development are unavailable; no resizing of a ready mature plant.
findings.evidenceScope: Selected actual university species diagnosis through search retrieval: variable shrubby/tree habit, awl leaves in whorls of three with one broad pale upper band, globose wax-bloomed blue/black fleshy seed cones. No ordinary flower/fruit interpretation.
corrections: Built a selected multistemmed shrub with secondary leafy axes, adult awl leaves in three-member whorls and fused blue-grey fleshy seed-cone cues.
Replaced overly white broad leaf faces with a narrower pale upper band and green margins after comparison with the privately viewed institutional close photograph.
Varied leaf orientations and grey woody pigmentation while retaining branch/leaf identity across sway.
findings.residual: The crown remains open and regularly repeated compared with the retained old shrub photograph. Fine band placement, wax bloom, tissue optics and proportions are unmeasured. Prostrate and tree habits, regional/subspecific concepts, cone maturation and seedling development are not represented as universal variation.
